title: Academic Task 1 - Describing maps
subtitle: Change over time, location language and tenses
summary: Describe what has changed on a map and what has stayed the same, using the right verb for each kind of change and the present perfect passive.

lesson.heading: Two maps means two questions
lesson.text: When you are given the same place at two dates, the examiner wants both halves of the story: **what has changed** and **what has stayed the same**. Work through the map feature by feature and note one or the other for each.

examples.text: the hotel - **has been expanded / extended**
Steggle Farm - **has been removed / is no longer there**
the roads - **have been modernised**; traffic lights and a roundabout **have been added**
Goode Farm - **has been replaced with a car park**
the stables - **have been demolished and replaced with a block of flats**
the market square, the church, the bridge, the row of shops - **have not changed**

lesson.note: Unchanged features are worth real marks. An answer listing only the new buildings has missed half the comparison.

lesson.heading: The verb tells the examiner what kind of change it is
rows: take something away and put something else in its place
build several buildings in an area where there was nothing
lesson.note: Choosing *replace* where you mean *renovate* is an accuracy error, not a style one - the two describe different things happening to the building.

lesson.heading: Say where things are
lesson.text: A map description needs location language on almost every line. Learn a handful of phrases and vary them.

examples.text: *The **market square**, which is **right in the centre** of the town, has not changed in 300 years.*
*According to the 1700s map, there was a **house** in the **bottom right-hand corner**.*
*Another feature that has remained the same is the **church**, located **in the centre, to the right of** the market square.*
*The row of **shops** that can be seen in the **bottom centre** of both maps has changed little.*
*Steggle Farm, which can be seen **at the bottom left / in the lower left-hand corner** of the 1700s map, is no longer there.*
*In the **top left-hand corner of** both maps, there is a bridge.*

lesson.heading: The two tenses a map answer runs on

left.label: The older map - past simple
examples: *In the 1700s, the town **was** relatively small and **consisted of** a few farms and houses.*
*Transport **was restricted** to horses at that time, so the roads **were** very basic.*
*In the 1700s there **were** stables located behind the church.*

right.label: The change - present perfect passive
examples: *Goode Farm **has** now **been replaced** with a car park.*
*The hotel **has been extended** and is now almost twice the size it was in 1700.*
*Traffic lights, a roundabout and a zebra crossing **have** now **been added**.*
*The stables **have been removed** and replaced with a block of flats.*

lesson.note: *Has been + past participle* is the single most useful structure in this task, because a map shows results rather than actions.

lesson.heading: Errors that a quick check would catch
lesson.text: Grammatical Accuracy is a criterion in its own right. In one sample answer, ten mistakes were all of the same few kinds.

examples.text: *The two maps **allows** us to see ...* - **allow**
*the town ... **consists** of a few farms* - **consisted**
*Transport **restricted** to horses* - **was restricted**
*a great deal **changing*** - **has changed**
*the roads **are improving*** - **have been improved**
*traffic lights ... **been adding*** - **have been added**
*a car park **now replaced** Goode Farm* - **has now replaced**
*the fields that **are locate*** - **are located**
*Housing is another area where many changes **are made*** - **have been made**
*the hotel, which **is extending*** - **has been extended**

lesson.text: Work out how much space 150 of your words takes on a page, so you never have to count in the exam. And practise with a timer set to 15 minutes - if you can write it in 15, you have 5 minutes left to check.

exercises.prompt: Match each verb with the change it describes.

pairs.right: put something else in its place
build on an area where there was nothing

exercises.prompt: *Goode Farm ___ with a car park.* (replace - present perfect passive)
exercises.explanation: A map shows the result of a change, which is exactly what the present perfect passive expresses.

exercises.prompt: Between 1700 and today, sort each feature of the town centre.

options: The two maps allows us to see the changes over a 300-year period.
The two maps allow us to see the changes over a 300-year period.
The two maps allowing us to see the changes over a 300-year period.
The two maps is allowing us to see the changes over a 300-year period.
exercises.explanation: *Maps* is plural, so the verb takes no -s. Subject-verb agreement is one of the commonest accuracy errors in this task.

exercises.statement: In a map description you should only write about the features that have changed.
exercises.explanation: Features that have stayed the same are part of the comparison, and the task asks you to make comparisons where relevant.

exercises.prompt: *In the 1700s, the town was relatively small and ___ of a few farms and houses.* (consist)
exercises.explanation: A finished period in the past takes the past simple, even though the sentence next to it may use the present perfect.

exercises.prompt: Build a sentence about a feature that has not changed.
exercises.answer: The market square, which is right in the centre of the town, has not changed in 300 years.
exercises.explanation: The relative clause adds the location without a second sentence - good for Grammatical Range as well as accuracy.

exercises.prompt: *The hotel ___ and is now almost twice the size it was in 1700.* Which form is correct?
exercises.explanation: The hotel did not extend itself, and the result is visible now - so present perfect passive.

exercises.prompt: Match each location phrase with where it points on a map.

pairs.left: to the right of the market square

exercises.statement: Using paragraphs in a Writing Task 1 answer shows that it is well organised.
exercises.explanation: Coherence and cohesion are marked in Task 1 as well as Task 2, and paragraphing is the clearest evidence of organisation.
